comment: The guest's pre-arrival dinner answer, as every screen must read it:
formDinnerCell in nala-shared.js, the one reader behind the Reservations
board, the SMS invitations page, the front desk and the printed sheet.
Found 4 Sep: each screen read its own subset of the fact and disagreed.
The suites evaluate the function inside their own loaded page against
every case here - the phone_cases.json pattern. Add cases HERE, not to a
suite: a case added here fails every screen that has not learned it.
rec.arriveOffset is days from the rendered night to the arrival: 0 is an
arrival that night, negative is mid-stay. arriveField says which spelling
the record uses - roomguests entries say `arrives`, raw /stays entries
say `arrive`, and the reader must honour both. expect is the returned
cell's telling fields, or null when the form must stay silent. What is
NOT here: a /dinner cell outranking all of this, which is each caller's
own precedence and asserted by each suite on its rendered page.

cases.name: dining on the form, arriving tonight, party and dietaries carried
declined on the form, arriving tonight
an abandoned form still counts - an answer given is an answer
no pax named: the booking's party size stands in
mid-stay: the form asked about the first night, not this one
arriving tomorrow: not tonight's answer either
a form with no dinner answer says nothing
no form at all says nothing
no arrival date on the record: no gate, so no answer
the raw /stays spelling `arrive` is honoured the same
